chapter: Opinions on singers, promotion and originality
title: Black music as America's culture and the promotion of rock and country
summary: Edison argues jazz is the only American culture, that rock is white music, and that only Norman Granz promotes jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I don't know who she sounds like. I think she's trying to sound like --
Well, that's a hard thing. But when she sings --now I know / with my kids, our daughter is 21 this next month. She really likes country music. You know, and you can't imagine why.
Well, they try to promote everything beside black music, Stanley. You know, the black music is the
only culture that America has. It is culture. It's an art. It's an art. Country music came way after the blues because cowboys came way after slavery, you know.
But the other thing is, it seems to me with what they've done with so-called soul music --

No, it isn't. But it seems to me as though they almost deliberately are trying to destroy that because -- or turn it into something which could be black or white. You know, Aretha Franklin had a big thing going but that seems to be over.
Yeah, well, rhythm and blues -- rock and roll is strictly white music.
Rock and roll, that's white music. Rhythm and blues, why they're trying to wash out everything, anyway, that is connected with the black art, which is music.

That's right. They will not promote it. You take a promoter, take any rock and roll group and promote them until they're the biggest thing that's ever happened. With no talent. Nothing. They have nothing to offer. You know, you keep promoting a piece of paper, people will buy it because they're curious. Everytime one rock and roll singer begins to diminish, they find somebody else to make him big, you know. But no talent

at all, you know. They can't do a damn thing. But they will not promote jazz, which is purely American. That's why I like the Europeans, because they do appreciate jazz. They appreciate you for what you have contributed to the world of culture. And jazz is a culture. Because anything that is originated, that is something that only a person can do that the whole world recognizes, that's an art. That's an art.
And they will not promote it. Like Norman is to only one I know that promotes jazz.

Norman Granz. He's the only one that I know that when he gives a concert, it is jazz all the way. It's all the way. I mean, it's strictly, purely culture, which is jazz music. But it belongs to the black man. And anything that belongs to the black man, there's always something to -- the white man gets something to counteract it. Because I guess, I don't know, we're all Americans, you know, and it is an American art and it's the only thing that Americans say -- America can say it is American. You can't say -- they had Michaelangelo way before America was discovered, they had Rembrandt, Van Gogh, they had the Mozarts, they had the Greeks were building buildings, the Egyptians were building the pyramids. That was the beginning of that, you know.
But the beginning of American culture was jazz.
